# tfcensus report scan

scan prints the per-account counts of a scan and its top findings, double-managed first,
then unmanaged. --category lists another category instead.

With --from it reads a file from tfcensus scan --format json. Without it, it reads the newest
snapshot in the scan cache and applies the current ownership rules to it, with no AWS call.
A snapshot older than cache.ttl is used anyway, with a warning. It is what the scan\_summary
tool of tfcensus mcp returns.

## Usage

```sh
tfcensus report scan [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--account` | AWS account ID | string |  |  | [`accounts.include`](/reference/config#accounts-include) |  |
| `--category` | list this category: managed, double-managed, unmanaged, other-iac, aws-managed, derived, ignored or undetermined (default: double-managed and unmanaged) | string |  | `managed`: one state manages it<br>`double-managed`: more than one state manages it<br>`unmanaged`: no state manages it<br>`other-iac`: CloudFormation, CDK, Pulumi or a Kubernetes controller owns it<br>`aws-managed`: AWS created it, or it is a default<br>`derived`: a child of a managed or derived resource<br>`ignored`: an ownership rule ignores it<br>`undetermined`: type unmapped, or the layer data is not enough |  |  |
| `--from` | scan JSON (default: the newest scan cache snapshot) | string |  |  |  |  |
| `--region` | AWS region, or global | string |  | 35 values; shell completion lists them | [`regions`](/reference/config#regions) |  |
| `--top` | findings to list, 1 to 500 | int | `50` |  |  |  |
| `--type` | CloudFormation or layer type glob, such as AWS::EC2::\* | string |  |  |  |  |

The [global flags](/cli/global-flags) work with every command.

## Output formats

`--format` accepts `tty`, `plain`, `json`. Without it, the format is `tty` when stdout is a terminal and `plain` otherwise. Formats are described on the [global flags](/cli/global-flags) page.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The command finished. With --fail-on, nothing matched. |
| 1 | The command failed: a read, a write, a child process or a check failed. |
| 2 | Wrong usage: an unknown command or flag, a bad value or argument, an invalid config file, or a prompt with no terminal. |
| 130 | Interrupted by Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or a cancelled context. |

All codes are listed on the [exit codes](/reference/exit-codes) page.

## Examples

```sh
tfcensus report scan --from scan.json --account 111111111111 --top 20
tfcensus report scan --category undetermined
```
